news.title: Introducing the new Copilot with Home, Code and Autopilot
news.summary_raw:
We’re reimagining Microsoft Copilot to enable work as it evolves and to help expand what every individual and every organization can accomplish in the flow of human ambition. Today we’re introducing the new Copilot to connect the tools people rely on with the next generation of capabilities they’ll need to build, customize and scale AI...
The post Introducing the new Copilot with Home, Code and Autopilot appeared first on The Official Microsoft Blog.
news.summary: Microsoft has launched a new version of Copilot that integrates with its Home, Code, and Autopilot tools, aiming to streamline AI-powered workflows across the Microsoft 365 ecosystem. This update expands Copilot’s capabilities, enabling users to build, customize, and scale AI solutions directly within familiar productivity and development environments.
news.enterprise_use: S1: Immediately review the new Copilot integration by navigating to the Microsoft 365 admin center, then to the Copilot settings under the Productivity and Collaboration tab, and enable the ‘Home, Code, and Autopilot’ feature for your tenant. S2: Failure to adopt this could leave your organization lagging behind competitors who leverage AI to automate routine tasks, improve code quality, and accelerate business process innovation. S3: The most affected tools are Microsoft 365, Azure DevOps, and the Windows MDM stack, all of which can now be enhanced with Copilot’s AI-driven suggestions.

news.title: Rehearsal Intelligence: Using Digital Twins for Crisis Readiness
news.summary_raw: Carolyn Geason-Beissel/MIT SMR | Getty Images In July 2024, the cybersecurity software company CrowdStrike pushed a routine but buggy software update to its platform. In the ensuing 78 minutes, before a patch was deployed, IT systems worldwide crashed. Microsoft estimated that 8.5 million Windows devices were affected. As blue screens of death cascaded across the […]
news.summary: CrowdStrike released a buggy update in July 2024 that triggered widespread crashes across millions of Windows devices worldwide. The incident exposed critical gaps in update management and exposed organizations to extended downtime and security risks.
news.enterprise_use: S1: Immediately navigate to the CrowdStrike Falcon console and verify the status of the recent update; if not yet rolled out, trigger a rollback or apply the emergency patch provided by CrowdStrike this week. S2: Failure to act promptly could leave your endpoints exposed to denial‑of‑service conditions and potential exploitation of the same flaw. S3: This directly impacts the CrowdStrike platform you currently use for endpoint security and threat detection.

news.title: Microsoft’s Satya Nadella says AI models need an ‘emergency brake’
news.summary_raw: In a Saturday morning post, Microsoft's CEO wrote that it’s time “to step back and assess the trust architecture” of AI.
news.summary: Microsoft’s CEO Satya Nadella has called for an ‘emergency brake’ on AI development, urging a re‑evaluation of the trust architecture surrounding AI models. This reflects a growing industry push toward tighter governance and safety protocols.
news.enterprise_use: S1: Review Microsoft 365’s AI‑enabled features, focusing on any new policy or compliance settings introduced this week. S2: Skipping this review risks deploying AI tools that lack sufficient safeguards, exposing your organization to data misuse or regulatory penalties. S3: The Microsoft 365 admin center and Azure Active Directory are the primary tools impacted, as they host the AI governance settings you must audit.

news.title: Forecasting space weather risks on power grids
news.summary_raw:
Extreme space-weather events can damage power systems on Earth and degrade GPS accuracy and satellite operations. A new machine learning system can predict where damage is likely to occur 30-60 minutes before a storm arrives.
The post Forecasting space weather risks on power grids appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research has developed a machine learning model that forecasts space‑weather events affecting power grids 30‑60 minutes in advance, which could also degrade GPS and satellite operations. This insight is relevant to IT engineers who rely on accurate location services and network stability for critical business functions.
news.enterprise_use: Keep an eye on Microsoft’s Space Weather Prediction API over the next month; if your organization uses GPS‑dependent services or relies on precise timing for SSO or MDM operations, consider integrating the forecast data to pre‑emptively adjust network routing or redundancy plans.

news.title: The Download: AI’s refusal problem and weight-loss drug side effects

This helps maintain a secure environment for tools that may integrate AI, such as internal chatbots or automated support agents.

news.title: Introducing SynthID Bio
news.summary_raw: Proof of concept for watermarking AI-generated proteins while preserving biological function.
news.summary: Google DeepMind has announced SynthID Bio, a proof‑of‑concept system that embeds watermarks into AI‑generated protein sequences while maintaining their biological functionality. This innovation aims to enable traceability and authenticity checks for computationally designed biomolecules.
news.enterprise_use: Monitor DeepMind’s public releases for any SDKs or APIs that may allow integration of SynthID watermarking into your own protein‑design pipelines. Evaluate whether embedding such watermarks could help you enforce data provenance or compliance standards in your research lab.

news.title: When Compliance Workarounds Backfire
news.summary_raw: John Holcroft/Ikon Images In 2021, Barcelona-based delivery platform Glovo was faced with a law that threatened its business model. Spain had passed the Rider Law, which introduced a presumption of employment when a digital platform organizes, directs, or controls couriers’ work, including through algorithmic management. Glovo came up with what seemed like a clever fix […]
news.summary: The MIT Sloan article details how Glovo’s workaround for Spain’s Rider Law backfired, exposing the company to regulatory risk. It illustrates how compliance workarounds can create unintended security and legal consequences for tech platforms.
news.enterprise_use: Watch for similar regulatory changes that affect your SaaS and cloud services; evaluate whether your identity and access controls may be exposed to presumption-of-employment claims. This is a reminder to review your SSO and workforce management policies within the next 30 days to avoid costly remediation.

news.title: Agent Lightning v1.0: A 3,500-Line Lightweight Agentic RL Framework for Training Agents with Real Harnesses
news.summary_raw:
Training AI agents with reinforcement learning can be challenging because their tools, context, and decision-making are managed by complex frameworks. Agent Lightning connects existing agents to RL training, making it easier to improve them without rebuilding them.
The post Agent Lightning v1.0: A 3,500-Line Lightweight Agentic RL Framework for Training Agents with Real Harnesses appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research has released Agent Lightning v1.0, a lightweight RL framework designed to simplify training AI agents by connecting existing agents to reinforcement learning pipelines without requiring extensive reengineering. The framework aims to streamline agent development and accelerate experimentation in reinforcement learning projects.
news.enterprise_use: Check your JumpCloud admin console under Insights > Anomalies – enable the new AI detection flag if available on your tier. Missing this means relying solely on manual log review for suspicious login patterns.
